mainTopic: Temurah 23b: Leftover sin-offering animals and money. The views of רב הונא and רבי אבא are defended, and רבי אמי's ruling on two backup piles of money is examined.
overview: This amud tests the views of רב הונא and רבי אבא about a lost חטאת that turns up after a replacement was set aside. First the גמרא says an earlier source follows only רבי, so it does not contradict רבי אבא. Then it brings two משניות, one about animals and one about money. Read closely, each seems to rule the same way in every case, which would refute both sages. Both times the גמרא answers that the משנה only teaches the clear-cut case and stays silent on cases that depend on other details. Next, רבי אמי rules that when someone sets aside two piles of money as a backup, the leftover pile goes to נדבה. The גמרא asks whose view needs this ruling and rejects רבי and the רבנן, since for them it is obvious. It says the ruling is needed for רבי שמעון, but then proves from the thirteen collection boxes and the teaching of יהוידע הכהן that רבי שמעון already holds of נדבה. The גמרא begins a new answer: maybe רבי שמעון allows נדבה only with one set of money. That answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does this source follow even the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the source it just quoted follows even the רבנן, which would contradict רבי אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it true that this source follows even the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a pointed question about the source it just brought. Does it follow even the רבנן? If it does, that is a problem for רבי אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the source follows even the רבנן, then even the רבנן treat the replacement animal like the lost one. רבי אבא's explanation of the רבנן's view does not allow for that. So the question is really a challenge to רבי אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it true that...? (a way of pushing for a reading that creates a problem)
The Rabbis, meaning the majority view of the sages

phrases.english: What, is it not that it follows even the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section by challenging how the earlier source should be read.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's account of the רבנן's position
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the source follows even the רבנן, it shows that even they treat the replacement like the lost animal. That contradicts רבי אבא.

steps.title: No, the source follows only רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the source follows רבי alone, so the רבנן may disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is the view of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question. The source follows רבי only, not the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the source is assigned to רבי alone, it says nothing about what the רבנן hold. So רבי אבא's explanation of the רבנן is still standing.

keyTerms.meaning: No (the answer turns down the suggested reading)

phrases.english: No, it is Rabbi.
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, whose opinion is argued against by the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to one תנא only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source might follow everyone, including the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source follows only רבי, so it does not contradict רבי אבא.

steps.title: The משנה: a lost sin offering after a replacement was sacrificed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if someone set aside a חטאת, it got lost, and he offered another in its place, the first one must die.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: One who sets aside a sin offering and it gets lost, and he sacrifices another in its place, the first must die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה. It is setting up a new challenge, this time against both רב הונא and רבי אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in the משנה is that the owner already got his atonement through the second animal. The original animal is then left to die. On its own this line is not yet a challenge. The challenge comes from the close reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside (dedicates) an animal for an offering
A sin offering
In its place, as its replacement
It must die (left alone until it dies, and never offered)

phrases.english: We learned: One who sets aside a sin offering and it was lost,
and he sacrificed another in its place,
it shall die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge, aimed at both רב הונא and רבי אבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a lost חטאת is found after a replacement was already offered, the found animal is left to die.

steps.title: Inference: before the replacement is offered, the animal grazes in every case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. The animal dies only because the replacement was already offered. Before that it grazes, no matter how the case looks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it dies is that he already sacrificed the replacement. But if he had not sacrificed it, the animal grazes. It makes no difference whether he gets atonement through the lost animal or through the animal that was not lost. And it makes no difference whether he took and offered it on his own or did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the exact wording of the משנה. Death depends only on whether the replacement was already offered. No other detail matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives one reason for death: the replacement was already offered. So if it was not yet offered, the animal grazes in every version of the case. That includes which animal he gets atonement with and whether he took it on his own. Those are exactly the details רב הונא and רבי אבא each said lead to death according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is... (used to show what a ruling depends on)
It shall graze until it gets a blemish, then it is sold
It makes no difference
Gets atonement through
Took (pulled) the animal to offer it, here meaning on his own, without the court

steps.confusionAlert: תמות (dies) and תרעה (grazes) are two different outcomes. With תרעה, the animal grazes until it gets a blemish and is then sold. With תמות, it is simply left to die. The whole question is which animal gets which outcome.

phrases.english: The reason is because he sacrificed it,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Both mean the replacement was already offered.

phrases.english: but if he did not sacrifice it, it shall graze,
no difference whether he gets atonement with the lost one,
no difference whether he gets atonement with the one that was not lost,
no difference whether he took it,
phrases.notes: He took it on his own and offered it, without asking the court.

phrases.english: and no difference whether he did not take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּהִקְרִיבָהּ, הָא לֹא הִקְרִיבָהּ — תִּרְעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a close-reading lesson from the משנה quoted in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רב הונא and רבי אבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Death depends only on the replacement having been offered. So the details each of them relied on to say 'everyone agrees it dies' make no difference.

steps.title: A refutation of both רב הונא and רבי אבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the משנה seems to refute both רב הונא and רבי אבא. The next step answers this.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the משנה seems to knock down both opinions. Step 6 will defend them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא held that everyone agrees the animal dies if the owner took one on his own. The משנה shows it makes no difference. רבי אבא held that everyone agrees the lost animal dies if he got atonement with the other one. The משנה shows that makes no difference either.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; the opinion is rejected
Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: Read closely, the משנה seems to say that only an offered replacement sends the found חטאת to die. That reading threatens both רב הונא and רבי אבא. The next step answers it.
steps.whyThisMatters: A תיובתא would normally mean these explanations are rejected. That is why the גמרא has to defend them in the next step.

phrases.english: A refutation of both of them!
phrases.notes: "Both" means רב הונא and רבי אבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the result of the challenge in Step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now it seems that both רב הונא and רבי אבא are refuted, since before the replacement is offered the found חטאת would graze no matter how the case looks. Step 6 rejects this and defends both views.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רב הונא and רבי אבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the found animal's death depend only on the replacement having been offered. That leaves no room for the cases where each of them said everyone agrees it dies.

steps.title: The משנה only teaches a clear-cut case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב הונא and רבי אבא. The משנה only mentions the case whose outcome never changes. It leaves out cases that depend on other details.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא teaches a case that is clear-cut. He does not teach a case that is not clear-cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the refutation from step 5. It explains that the משנה chose to teach only the case with a single, fixed outcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the גמרא read the משנה as saying: before the replacement is offered, the lost animal always grazes, no matter what. The answer here is that the משנה simply did not discuss the in-between cases. It taught the case where the replacement was already offered, because there the first animal always dies. Cases whose outcome depends on other details were left out, so there is room for רב הונא and רבי אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear-cut matter: a case with one fixed outcome
A matter that is not clear-cut: the outcome depends on other details
He (the תנא) teaches

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying the other cases have no special rule. It just chose not to discuss them, so silence here is not a ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic tool. A precise reading of a משנה can be answered by saying the תנא only spelled out the case with a fixed outcome.

phrases.english: A matter that is clear-cut for him, he teaches;

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא דְּלָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ — לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: a matter that is not clear-cut for him, he does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation stated in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: The תנא chose to teach only the clear-cut case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's silence means the lost animal always grazes until the replacement is offered
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only addresses the fixed-outcome case, so the other cases stay open

steps.title: A משנה about lost money for a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. Someone set aside money for a חטאת, lost it, set aside new money, and then found the old money. He combines both to buy a חטאת, and the leftover goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If someone sets aside money for a חטאת, and it is lost, and he sets aside other money instead, and then the first money is found, he brings a חטאת from both sets of money, and the rest goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge by quoting another משנה. The next steps will read this משנה closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case matches the earlier one about animals, but with money. Now two sets of money exist for one חטאת. The משנה's solution is to use some of both and send whatever is left to נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside or designates
Money (coins)
In their place, as a replacement
A gift offering, a voluntary sacrifice

phrases.english: We learned: One who sets aside money for a sin offering,
and it was lost, and he set aside other money in its place,
and afterward the original money was found:
he should bring a sin offering from this money and that money,
and the remainder goes to gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to challenge רב הונא and רבי אבא again
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If both sets of money exist, he brings a חטאת from both and the rest goes to נדבה

steps.title: Reading the משנה closely: otherwise the money is destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the leftover goes to נדבה only because he used both sets of money. If he used just one, the other must be thrown into the Dead Sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the rest goes to gift offerings is that he gains atonement from both. But if he used just one, he must take the other money to the Dead Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and draws out what it implies when he uses only one set of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a good outcome (נדבה) only when both sets are mixed. So if he gains atonement with one set alone, the other set is left over from a חטאת already brought, and it must be destroyed. That inference becomes the basis for the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason (introduces a close reading of a source)
He gains atonement
The Dead Sea, where money is thrown to destroy it

phrases.english: The reason is that he gains atonement from both this and that;
but if from one of them, he must take the others to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: Throwing it into the Dead Sea is how you get rid of money that can't be used, so no one benefits from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the משנה quoted in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The views of רב הונא and רבי אבא (developed in the next step)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies the leftover is always destroyed when only one set is used

steps.title: No difference in any case: a refutation of both
steps.stepSummary: The inference seems to apply in every situation. It does not matter which money he used, or whether he took it on his own. That would refute both רב הונא and רבי אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes no difference whether he gained atonement with the lost money or the money that was not lost. It makes no difference whether he took it on his own or not. This is a refutation of both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses the inference. Since the משנה makes no distinctions, it seems to clash with both רב הונא and רבי אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's view depends on whether the owner 'took' it on his own (משך), without asking the court. רבי אבא's view depends on which one he used for atonement: the lost one or the other one. The משנה, read plainly, gives one result for every situation: destroy the extra money. So it seems to contradict both.

keyTerms.meaning: The lost one

phrases.english: There is no difference whether he gains atonement with the lost one,
or whether he gains atonement with the one that was not lost,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא מָשַׁךְ, וְלָא שְׁנָא לֹא מָשַׁךְ —
phrases.english: and no difference whether he took it or did not take it;
phrases.notes: 'Took it' means he went ahead and used it on his own, without first asking the court.

phrases.english: this is a refutation of both of them!
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means רב הונא and רבי אבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the inference of step 8 into a refutation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה applies one rule in every case, which leaves no room for their distinctions

steps.title: Same answer: only the clear-cut case is taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. The משנה teaches only the clear-cut case and leaves out cases that depend on other details.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the תנא teaches a case that is clear-cut, and does not teach a case that is not clear-cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the answer from step 6 and uses it against this second challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only spoke about the case where the outcome never changes. The cases that depend on which money he used, or whether he took it on his own, were simply not discussed. So the משנה does not contradict רב הונא or רבי אבא, and both views survive.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too

steps.whatToRemember: Two refutations of רב הונא and רבי אבא were answered the same way: a משנה teaches the clear-cut case and stays silent on cases that depend on other details.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: מִילְּתָא דִּפְסִיקָא לֵיהּ קָתָנֵי,
phrases.english: Here too: a matter that is clear-cut for him, he teaches,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִילְּתָא דְּלָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: and a matter that is not clear-cut for him, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי מִילְּתָא דִּפְסִיקָא לֵיהּ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 9 using the answer from step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: The תנא chose to teach only the clear-cut case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires destroying the extra money in every case
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only covers the fixed-outcome case, so the views of רב הונא and רבי אבא stand
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רב הונא and רבי אבא survive, since the משנה does not address cases that depend on other details

steps.title: רבי אמי: Two Backup Piles of Money
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that if someone sets aside two piles of money as a guarantee for one חטאת, he uses one pile, and the other goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי says: One who sets aside two piles of money as a backup gains atonement with one of them, and the second goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אמי about money set aside for a חטאת as a backup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person sets aside both piles at the same time, on purpose, so that one can replace the other if it gets lost. Nothing was actually lost. רבי אמי says the extra pile is not destroyed; it goes to buy communal gift offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Piles of money
As a guarantee or backup, in case one gets lost
Gains atonement through his offering
Gift offerings; here, communal offerings bought with leftover money

steps.confusionAlert: This is different from the earlier case in steps 7-10. There the first money was lost and new money was set aside to replace it. Here both piles were set aside together as a backup, and nothing was lost.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami says:
One who sets aside two piles of money as a guarantee,
phrases.notes: One pile for his חטאת, and the second as a spare in case the first gets lost.

phrases.english: gains atonement with one of them,
and the second goes to gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: הַמַּפְרִישׁ שְׁנֵי צִיבּוּרֵי מָעוֹת לְאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: money set aside as a backup, not as a replacement for lost money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of two piles of money set aside as a backup for one חטאת, one is used and the leftover goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Whose Opinion Is This?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's view רבי אמי's ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion רבי אמי is following. This sets up the next steps, where it tests each possible opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real question is why רבי אמי needed to say this at all. If his ruling is already obvious under a certain opinion, it would not need to be taught for that opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion step 11 follows, in order to see why it needed to be said.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion רבי אמי's ruling is needed for.

steps.title: According to רבי, It Is Obvious
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אמי follows רבי, his ruling is obvious. רבי only sends the money to the Dead Sea when it replaced lost money, and he agrees about money set aside as a backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it follows רבי, it is obvious that the leftover goes to gift offerings. רבי only spoke about one who sets aside money to replace lost money. But about a backup, he agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries saying רבי אמי follows רבי, and shows that this makes his ruling unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's strict view, that leftover money is thrown away, applies only to money set aside after the first money was lost. In a backup case nothing was lost, and רבי agrees the leftover goes to נדבה. So there is no new lesson here according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion the גמרא will reject)
It is obvious, so why teach it?
He only said his view up to this point, meaning only in this case
Setting aside money to replace money that was lost
He agrees

phrases.english: If you say it follows Rebbi,
it is obvious that it goes to gift offerings,
for Rebbi only said his view
about one who sets aside money for lost money,
but about a backup, he agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 12 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי אמי follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי already agrees the leftover goes to נדבה in a backup case, so רבי אמי would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: According to the רבנן, It Is Even More Obvious
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אמי follows the רבנן, his ruling is obvious through a קל וחומר. They give money to נדבה even when it replaced lost money, so surely they do so in a backup case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows the רבנן? Then it is obvious to them that it goes to gift offerings, by a קל וחומר. Now, the רבנן said that one who sets aside money for lost money does not treat it like lost money. Is it even a question about a backup?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries saying רבי אמי follows the רבנן, and shows that his ruling is still unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן are lenient even in the harder case, where money replaced lost money. They say it goes to נדבה and is not thrown away. If so, in the easier backup case they would surely say the same, so there is again nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if it is true in the harder case, it is surely true in the easier case
Now that this is true, do we even need to ask about that?
It is not treated like lost money

phrases.english: Rather, it follows the Rabbis?
Then it is obvious to them that it goes to gift offerings,
by a kal vachomer:
Now, one who sets aside money for lost money,
the Rabbis said it is not treated like lost money,
is it even a question about a backup?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible answer to step 12 and rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי אמי follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the replacement case already proves the backup case, so the ruling teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Needed for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי's ruling is needed for רבי שמעון. We might have thought he holds no נדבה at all, and רבי אמי teaches that he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was needed according to רבי שמעון. You might have said that רבי שמעון does not hold of gift offerings. So it teaches us that he does hold of gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: רבי אמי's ruling is needed for the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is strict with leftover animals. Even when they were set aside as a backup, he says the extra one is left to die. We might have thought he is equally strict with money and never allows נדבה. רבי אמי teaches that with money set aside as a backup, even רבי שמעון agrees the leftover goes to נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed (to be taught)
You might have said (a mistaken assumption)
It teaches us (the new point)
He does not hold of / he does hold of

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's ruling teaches that money set aside as a backup goes to נדבה even according to רבי שמעון, who is strict about leftover animals.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a strict rule about animals does not automatically carry over to money set aside as a backup.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rather, it was needed according to Rabbi Shimon.
You might have said
that Rabbi Shimon does not hold of gift offerings,
so it teaches us
that he does hold of gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 12, after steps 13 and 14 rejected רבי and the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to a specific opinion where it adds a new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון, who is strict with backup animals, would not allow leftover backup money to go to נדבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי שמעון holds that leftover backup money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: Challenge: Can we really say רבי שמעון has no נדבה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the last answer. It brings the משנה about thirteen collection boxes in the מקדש, six of which were for נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you really say that רבי שמעון does not hold of נדבה? Isn't it taught: There were thirteen collection boxes in the מקדש. Written on them were: 'New shekels' and 'Old shekels', 'Bird pairs' and 'Young birds for עולה', 'Wood', 'Frankincense', and 'Gold for the כפרת'. And six were for נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer from Step 15. To do this, it starts quoting a source about the collection boxes in the מקדש, which leads into the proof in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said we might have thought רבי שמעון holds of no נדבה at all. The גמרא asks how anyone could think that. The משנה shows there was a whole system of six boxes set aside for נדבה, and the next steps will show that רבי שמעון agrees to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Collection boxes shaped like horns: narrow at the top, wide at the bottom
New shekels: the half-shekel given for the current year
Old shekels: a half-shekel given late, for last year
Pairs of birds brought as required offerings
The gold cover on top of the ארון

phrases.english: But can you really say
that רבי שמעון does not hold of נדבה?
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 15, which said we might have thought this about רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
There were thirteen collection boxes in the מקדש,
and written on them was:
'New shekels' and 'Old shekels',
'Bird pairs' and 'Young birds for an עולה',
'Wood' and 'Frankincense'
and 'Gold for the כפרת',
and six were for נדבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּלֵית לֵיהּ נְדָבָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 15 that one might think רבי שמעון holds of no נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known source shows a נדבה system that רבי שמעון accepts, so no one could have thought he rejects נדבה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains the six נדבה boxes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the six boxes paid for עולות bought from leftover money. According to רבי יהודה, the hides of these עולות did not go to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught about this: 'Six for נדבה' means for an עולה that comes from leftover money, and its hide does not go to the כהנים. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains what the six נדבה boxes were for. This sets up the argument that comes next, where רבי שמעון's view appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover money, for example from a חטאת or אשם, is used to buy עולות for the מזבח. רבי יהודה adds that the hides of these עולות are not given to the כהנים. That detail about the hides is what the next opinion will argue with.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover money that was not needed for its first purpose
A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
Its hide (the animal's skin)

phrases.english: And it was taught about it:
'Six for נדבה'
means for an עולה that comes from leftover money,
whose hide does not go to the כהנים,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the six נדבה boxes from the משנה in Step 16
steps.raayaObject: That leftover money is used for נדבה עולות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the משנה of the thirteen boxes, giving רבי יהודה's view

steps.title: רבי נחמיה (some say רבי שמעון) argues using the teaching of יהוידע הכהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה, or according to some רבי שמעון, objects that רבי יהודה's view cancels יהוידע's teaching. יהוידע taught that leftover חטאת and אשם money buys עולות, and the hides go to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him, and some say it was רבי שמעון: If so, you have cancelled the teaching of יהוידע הכהן. As it is taught: This is what יהוידע הכהן taught. The פסוק says 'It is an אשם', and also that it is entirely for ה׳. This comes to include anything that comes from leftover money of חטאות and אשמות: with that money we buy עולות. The meat goes to ה׳, and the hides go to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key proof. רבי שמעון (in one version) argues with רבי יהודה only about the hides, and in doing so shows that he agrees leftover money buys עולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says the hides go to the כהנים, like every regular עולה. But he never questions the main idea that leftover חטאת and אשם money is used for עולות. That main idea is exactly what נדבה means, so רבי שמעון clearly holds of נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from the words of a פסוק
The כהן גדול in the time of the kings, whose teaching about leftover money is quoted here
A guilt offering
Leftover money set aside for חטאות and אשמות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the argument about the hides. The גמרא only cares that both sides agree leftover money buys עולות. That shared point is what proves רבי שמעון holds of נדבה.

phrases.english: רבי נחמיה said to him,
and some say it was רבי שמעון:
If so, you have cancelled the teaching
of יהוידע הכהן.
As it is taught:
This is the teaching that יהוידע הכהן taught:
'It is an אשם', and it is entirely for Hashem,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:19. The פסוק calls it an אשם but also says it is 'for ה׳', so he reads it as something that goes completely to ה׳.

phrases.english: to include anything that comes
from leftover money of חטאות and אשמות,
that with its money we buy עולות:
the meat goes to ה׳,
and the hides go to the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִם כֵּן, בָּטְלָה מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's view from Step 17, and in doing so shows what רבי שמעון holds
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds leftover חטאת money goes to נדבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's use of יהוידע's teaching, which says leftover חטאת and אשם money buys עולות

steps.title: So רבי שמעון does hold of נדבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the conclusion: רבי שמעון holds of נדבה. So why would רבי אמי's ruling be needed for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that רבי שמעון does hold of נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. Since רבי שמעון clearly holds of נדבה, the answer in Step 15 seems to fall apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said רבי אמי's ruling was needed to teach that רבי שמעון holds of נדבה. We now see that this was already known from the ברייתא. So רבי אמי's ruling again looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see; this word draws a conclusion from a source

phrases.english: So we see that he holds of נדבה,
רבי שמעון does.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא אִית לֵיהּ נְדָבָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in Step 18 and turns it against Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 15 that רבי אמי's ruling is needed for רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון is already known to hold of נדבה, so רבי אמי adds nothing for him.

steps.title: Still needed: maybe רבי שמעון holds of נדבה only with one set of money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אמי's ruling is still needed. We might have thought רבי שמעון holds of נדבה only when the leftover comes from one set of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: when רבי שמעון holds of נדבה, that is only with one set of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to defend רבי אמי's ruling again. It sets up a mistaken idea, and the explanation of that idea continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer accepts that רבי שמעון holds of נדבה. But it narrows where he holds it: maybe only when there is one set of money that has some left over, for example because prices dropped. רבי אמי's case is different, because it has two separate piles of money, so his ruling teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed; this word defends a ruling as teaching something new
You might have thought; this introduces a mistaken first idea
One set (of money), meaning a single amount that was set aside

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא saves a ruling: it agrees with the general rule but shows the ruling teaches a new case that we might have treated differently.

phrases.english: It was needed,
phrases.notes: רבי אמי's ruling about the two piles of money is still needed, even for רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: because you might have thought:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִית לֵיהּ נְדָבָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: when רבי שמעון holds of נדבה,
that is only with one set of money,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 16-19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: רבי שמעון's נדבה might apply only to one set of money, not to two separate piles
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון holds of נדבה only when the leftover comes from one set of money
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי teaches that רבי שמעון holds of נדבה even with two separate piles (this conclusion is completed in the next lines)
